**The engines agree on the shape and disagree on four things.**

1. **Announcement content — the substantive disagreement.** Codex recommends a short string that points at `just --list` and names `cargo build` and `cargo test` as direct Rust alternatives, and its acceptance check asserts all four tokens are present. Opus recommends naming the `just` recipes with parenthetical purposes, forbids raw `cargo` commands, and adds the A4b drift gate. **Settled for Opus's vocabulary and Codex's index pointer**, on three pieces of evidence rather than on preference: F176 fixes `just` as the task-runner tool; R42's resolved `package-manager-invocation` value establishes that recipes invoke `cargo` directly, which makes `cargo` the layer beneath the interface the repository asks contributors to use; and a recipe name is checkable against `just --summary` where a `cargo` command is not. Codex's motivating concern — that a hard-coded recipe inventory goes stale — is real, is the reason the `just --list` pointer is kept, and is answered by A4b rather than by dropping recipe names. This is a proposal: P03 owns the final recipe set and the final string, and A4b is the check that keeps either choice safe.
2. **How much the announcement mechanism should be doubted, and on what.** Codex lowers its confidence to medium partly on "a user report [that] has alleged a visibility failure in one past version", citing `anthropics/claude-code` issue #22425. **That report is real, and revision 1 of this decision was wrong to deny it.** Revision 1 asserted that the issue "never mentions `companyAnnouncements`". It does: under its `## Current Behavior` heading the body reads "`companyAnnouncements` also doesn't display visibly", and its Environment block names Claude Code v2.1.21. The reporter's later comments do not withdraw that line. Codex's narrower statement is therefore supported by its own citation, and the sentence that dismissed it is withdrawn. **What the report weighs, stated no more strongly than it is.** It is one user's account of one version, seven months before this decision, inside an issue whose subject is a feature request rather than a bug report: opened 2026-02-01T18:58:49Z and closed `completed` by the reporter at 2026-02-01T19:03:37Z, after a duplicate-detection bot comment and two comments by the reporter (metadata Tier V, check 7). The body does not say at which scope the key was set, and the vendor documentation in evidence records no such failure. It is also contradicted by the later report Opus cites, #39998 ("[BUG] companyAnnoucements override", opened 2026-03-27, closed `not_planned` 2026-04-30), whose reporter runs Claude Code 2.1.85, creates "a project's settings file with companyAnnouncements message", and does see it displayed — the complaint being that it is framed as if it came from the company. That later report is not the clean-profile case either: that reporter's enterprise `managed-settings.json` already sets the key, so it evidences the merged case only. Two single reports at different versions, pointing opposite ways, are exactly why U2 stays open and why it asks for both profiles. **What this changes.** Codex's derived runner-up — "omit the field if an integration test proves it is not visibly displayed" — is no longer dismissed. It is the natural response to a negative U2, and it is recorded there with the one correction research must make to it: research cannot take that option unilaterally, because F199 is the owner requirement recorded in D-024(6), so a negative U2 goes to the owner. **What this does not change.** The display claim stays Tier D — documented scope, plus one organisation adopter, plus the merged-case report, against zero Rust adopters and one contrary historical report — and the single-entry rule and "nothing required lives only here" remain its mitigations. The recommendation is unchanged. The thread's other content still corroborates the *audience* split that decides this member, in the reporter's own words: "I'm seeing the `SessionStart` hook output appear correctly now. The hook output is captured and displayed as a `<system-reminder>` tag in Claude's context" — and, in the same comment, "the original request for a **user-visible terminal message** (not just context for Claude) may still be valuable". That is one user reporting exactly what Anthropic's hooks page documents: the hook reaches the model, not the human. Codex's third citation, #32221, is substantively right but is closed `not_planned`, not open. **Evidence and its tier.** The three issues' metadata is Tier V (check 7 of the 37). The body and comment text quoted in this paragraph is not: it was read directly with `gh api` on 2026-09-10 and snapshotted to `review/evidence/issue-22425.r2.json`, `review/evidence/issue-22425-comments.r2.json` and `review/evidence/issue-39998.r2.json`, none of which the 37-assertion script reads. Revision 1 labelled those direct reads Tier V; that label is withdrawn with the claim it supported.
3. **`BASELINE-REVIEW:` lines.** Codex emits two (F198 and F199); Opus emits none. **Neither is forwarded, and this decision carries no `BASELINE-REVIEW:` line.** `docs/port/BASELINE-REVIEW.md` scopes the mechanism to `COMMON → REUSE` and `ADOPT` rows — rows an item does *not* own and would otherwise inherit unchallenged. Both engines agree that F197 is **re-confirmed rather than challenged**, and Anthropic's memory page supplies the new corroboration: "Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`. If your repository already uses `AGENTS.md` for other coding agents, create a `CLAUDE.md` that imports it so both tools read the same instructions without duplicating them" (Tier V, retrieved 2026-09-10).

R43 decides the `companyAnnouncements` key and makes no claim about `enabledPlugins` or `extraKnownMarketplaces`.

A fifth difference is a factual correction too small to be a disagreement: Opus reports that `docs.cursor.com/context/rules` 308-redirects to `cursor.com/docs/rules`; the probe run on 2026-09-10 observed it resolving to `cursor.com/docs`. The point Opus drew from it — that Cursor reorganises its documentation, so a spoke's frontmatter contract is a moving target — is unaffected.

fixed.msrv-policy: stable minus 2 minor versions, raised only in a minor release, declared as rust-version in Cargo.toml and tested in CI

principles:
**Shared requirement, its source and agreement level.** One canonical, version-controlled statement of how to work in this repository, discoverable by whichever AI coding tool a contributor happens to use, with no second place where the same policy can drift; and, beside it, a repository-scoped greeting that tells a human what the project is and which commands to run. The first half is F197's principle (`docs/port/COMMONALITY.md:201`, `COMMON → REUSE`), already agreed and not re-decided here. The second half is the owner requirement recorded in the prompt's Context via D-024(6).

Two agreement levels are in play, and conflating them is the error the ts precedent invites:

| Concern | Agreement level | Must agree across py / ts / rs? |
|---|---|---|
| A single canonical instruction file exists and no second file restates its policy | architectural pattern | **Yes** — this is F197, already `COMMON → REUSE` |
| Which vendor rule paths are committed (`.cursor/`, `.windsurf/`, `.devin/`) | policy/mechanism | **No** — it may vary with each repository's contributor tooling and each vendor's current discovery behaviour |
| A repository-scoped welcome greets a human at session start | capability/standard, and an explicit owner requirement | **Yes** for the capability; the mechanism is per-tool |
| Which commands the welcome names | policy/mechanism, derived from F176 (`task-runner tool` = `just`, `COMMON → REUSE`) | **No** — each ecosystem names its own recipes |

That table is why the recommendation is *identical* to py (which ships neither spoke) and a *removal* relative to ts, without either repository being the winner by default: the removal is justified by the vendors' current documentation and by the practice evidence, not by py's agreement. py reached the same shape independently, in commit `fc8d944b7e439bb4e3f19aaf1b2bdf8da4292a57` — "docs(agents): make agents.md canonical; claude.md imports it; drop vendor rule files (#410)", pre-pin (Tier V, `git -C ~/c/py-launch-blueprint show --stat fc8d944`, 2026-09-10).

**Essential behaviours.** These are requirements the template must exhibit, recorded for P03 to prove. None has been observed on the rs template, which does not exist. B1 in particular is a requirement on third-party products, so it stays Tier D until P03 runs the check A5 describes.

- **B1.** A contributor's tool loads the repository's instructions without the contributor configuring anything.
- **B2.** Exactly one place holds a policy statement; every other file either points at it or does not exist.
- **B3.** A human opening a Claude Code session in this repository sees, once, what the project is and which commands to run.
- **B4.** No committed file can silently go stale relative to the commands or paths it names.

**Observable acceptance criteria.** A1 is F197's and is carried here only as the precondition R43 assumes; A2–A4 are R43's, and all four are for P03 to observe on the real template — none has been observed there, because the template does not exist.

- **A1.** `AGENTS.md` exists at the repository root, and `CLAUDE.md` contains an `@AGENTS.md` import and no independent policy statements.
- **A2.** `git ls-files` returns zero paths under `.cursor/`, `.windsurf/` or `.devin/`.
- **A3.** `.claude/settings.json` parses as JSON and `companyAnnouncements` is an array of exactly length 1.
- **A4a.** That single string names the repository and at least one `just` recipe.
- **A4b.** Every `just <recipe>` token the string contains appears in the output of `just --summary`.
- **A5.** Tier P, and not assertable in CI: opening the built template in Cursor, in Devin Desktop and in Devin CLI shows the root `AGENTS.md` in the agent's context; starting Claude Code in it shows the announcement to the human, both on a clean profile and on a profile that already sets `companyAnnouncements` at user or managed scope.

**What must agree versus what may vary.** Must agree: that exactly one file holds policy, that every tool reaches it, and that a human greeting exists. May vary: which vendor paths (if any) a given repository commits, and which recipe names its greeting lists. Naming the same recipe names in all three repositories would be a shared low-level value with no evidence supporting the same tradeoff in all three ecosystems, so this decision does not recommend one.

**Architectural alternatives, compared before any file was chosen.** Four designs are candidates for B1–B3. Each is assessed against the vendors' documented behaviour (Tier D), because none of them can be assessed by execution inside this programme.

| Design | How a vendor tool reaches the instructions | Files committed | Policy sources | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **D1. Hub-only** — root `AGENTS.md` plus `CLAUDE.md` importing it | Cursor, Devin Desktop and Devin CLI each *document* reading root `AGENTS.md` (Tier D); Claude Code documents reading `CLAUDE.md` | 2 | 1 | **Selected** |
| **D2. Hub + thin vendor spokes** (the ts shape) | Same as D1, plus one rule file per vendor whose body re-points at the hub | 2 + n | 1 policy file + n vendor frontmatter contracts | Not selected — the spoke buys nothing D1 lacks, and its own correctness is Tier P |
| **D3. Hub + substantive vendor rules** (the `surrealdb/surrealdb` shape) | Same as D1, plus vendor rules carrying their own content | 2 + n | n + 1 — **violates B2** | Excluded on principle. This is the shape py deliberately removed in `fc8d944` |
| **D4. Hub + nested `AGENTS.md`** for directory-scoped guidance | Cursor documents nested `AGENTS.md` as automatically applied and combined with parent directories; Devin documents a subdirectory `AGENTS.md` as a glob rule with an auto-generated `<directory>/**` pattern | 2 + k, all one format | 1 format, no vendor frontmatter | **Held in reserve.** This is the replacement for a glob-scoped rule file, and the answer to the workspace-shape argument |

D2 versus D1 is the real question, and D1 wins on three grounds, each stated at its own tier.

1. **The spoke instructs a tool to do what its documentation says it already does** (Tier D for the behaviour, Tier V for the documentation text). A body whose entire content is "read `AGENTS.md`" adds no instruction the hub does not already carry.
2. **The spoke is a second frontmatter contract that only the vendor controls, and its correctness is Tier P.** ts's `.cursor/rules/doc-template.mdc` writes `globs` as a YAML sequence (`- "docs/**/*.md"`), while Cursor's current page says "Use `globs` to scope a rule to specific files or directories. Separate multiple patterns with commas"; ts's `.cursor/rules/projectenv.mdc` writes `read rules ./doc-template.mdc` where the documented include form is `@filename`. Both file contents and both documentation strings are Tier V (re-read from the pin and from the live page on 2026-09-10). **Neither is evidence that current Cursor rejects those files** — that would require executing Cursor. They are recorded here exactly as Opus recorded them: *format drift observed against current vendor documentation, not verified by execution.* The point they establish is narrower and more useful than a breakage finding: a spoke's correctness can only ever be settled by running the vendor's product, so it can never be gated in CI, whereas the hub's format has no vendor frontmatter to drift.
3. **The directory-scoping argument is answered by the hub format, on the same documented basis (Tier D).** ts's `.windsurf/rules/justfile-rules.md` uses `trigger: glob` with `globs: Justfile` (Tier V, read from the pin). Both vendors now document nested `AGENTS.md` as providing directory scoping (D4, Tier D). It does not provide *single-file* scoping — but a root-level `Justfile`'s conventions land in the always-on root hub either way, and for a rule of roughly 30 lines the context saved by a glob trigger is negligible against the cost of a second policy source restating conventions F177 and F178 already record as `just`-native.

The one capability D1 gives up is the ability to hand a tool instructions the hub should not contain. The vendor's own current answer to that is a skill, not a rule file: "**To improve coding ability, speed of completion, and lower cost**, we highly recommend **using Skills instead whenever possible**. … **Rules and AGENTS should be kept as small as possible**" (Devin CLI rules page, Tier V, retrieved 2026-09-10). That is the documented escape hatch if a future need appears, and it is not this item's decision.

**Why the announcement is a separate mechanism and not a fourth spoke.** Claude Code exposes two session-start surfaces with different audiences, and they do not substitute for one another (all Tier V for the documentation text, retrieved 2026-09-10):

| Mechanism | Audience | What the documentation says |
|---|---|---|
| `companyAnnouncements` | **Human**, at startup | "Show your organization's announcements to users at startup. When you list more than one, Claude Code picks one at random for each session; on a person's very first launch it shows the first entry." Scope `Any file`; type array of strings; default unset |
| `SessionStart` hook → `additionalContext` | **Agent** | The string "passes … into Claude's context window", wrapped in a system reminder; a successful hook's "stdout is never shown in the transcript"; and the same page directs "For static context that doesn't require a script, use [CLAUDE.md](/docs/en/memory) instead" |

Only the first puts repository-scoped text in front of a human at session start, so the hook is the wrong tool for F199 by Anthropic's own guidance — even though `astral-sh/ruff` and `astral-sh/uv` are maintained Rust reference implementations of the hook path, because both use it for dynamic *agent* context, a different requirement (Tier V: `astral-sh/ruff`'s settings carry `hooks`, `enabledPlugins` and `extraKnownMarketplaces`; `astral-sh/uv`'s carry `hooks`; neither carries `companyAnnouncements`).

**Two documented semantics govern the announcement's shape, and both were re-read.** The settings page states "When you set the same list key … in more than one file, Claude Code combines the lists instead of picking one", exempting four model-list keys (`fallbackModel`, `modelPicker`, `availableModels`, `modelSettings`) of which `companyAnnouncements` is not one; and the reference states the random pick quoted above (Tier V, retrieved 2026-09-10). Chained, they give the consequence that governs the design: for a contributor whose organisation or user settings already set the key, the repository's welcome merges into that pool and is shown roughly one session in N, framed as a company message. The two design responses are (a) keep the repository's array at exactly one entry, so the template never multiplies the pool on its own, and (b) treat the welcome as a convenience and never as the only place a required instruction appears — anything a contributor must know belongs in `AGENTS.md`, which is loaded every session regardless.

**The MEDIUM question — `just` recipes, or `cargo` commands?** Name **`just` recipes**, plus `just --list` as the index; do not name raw `cargo` commands as a parallel vocabulary. Three reasons. F176 fixes `just` as the template's task-runner tool (`docs/port/COMMONALITY.md:180`, `COMMON → REUSE`). R42's resolved `package-manager-invocation` value settles that recipes invoke `cargo` subcommands directly with no provisioner prefix, so `cargo` is precisely the layer *beneath* the one the repository asks a contributor to use; naming it in the welcome teaches past the interface and duplicates the hub's command card in a third place. And a recipe name is checkable where a `cargo` command is not: `just --summary` enumerates recipes, so a welcome that names them can be gated against drift (A4b). The `just --list` pointer is carried from the Codex raw because it costs nothing and it keeps the welcome useful when the recipe set outgrows the string.

**The LOW question — staleness.** The announcement is the one member of this bundle with a real staleness risk, because it hard-codes recipe names P03 has not chosen. That risk is answered by making the check executable (A4b), not by omitting the welcome. The vendor-rule members' staleness risk is the opposite case: it is *not* checkable at all, since only the vendor's product can say whether a rule file still parses and still applies. That asymmetry — checkable drift kept, uncheckable drift removed — is the single principle that decides both halves of this bundle in opposite directions.

**Minimal realistic example (illustrative, not the final text; P03 owns the recipe list).** This decision authored no such file and did not write one to the tree:

```json
{
  "companyAnnouncements": [
    "rs-launch-blueprint: a production-ready Rust template shipping a CLI, a library crate and an optional web service behind a Cargo feature. Commands: just all (format, lint, typecheck, test), just check-deps (toolchain check), just debug-info (environment report); just --list for the rest. See AGENTS.md for the project charter and the Justfile for all recipes."
  ]
}
```

**Reference implementations.** For the recommended hub-only state, among maintained Rust projects that carry root `AGENTS.md` and no vendor rule directory: `rust-lang/rust`, `astral-sh/ruff`, `astral-sh/uv`, `nushell/nushell` and `meilisearch/meilisearch` (Tier V, re-checked 2026-09-10 in the 12-repository subset); Opus's wider census adds `rust-lang/rust-analyzer`, `zed-industries/zed`, `oxc-project/oxc`, `biomejs/biome`, `tikv/tikv`, `risingwavelabs/risingwave`, `vectordotdev/vector` and others (attributed to Opus, 2026-09-10, not re-derived here). `astral-sh/ruff`, `astral-sh/uv` and `biomejs/biome` additionally carry a `.claude/settings.json` beside that hub, which demonstrates that the exact file set this recommendation produces — `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/settings.json`, no vendor rule directory — coexists in maintained Rust repositories (Tier V). For the `companyAnnouncements` key specifically there is **no Rust reference implementation**: `ts@cb1cbcb2` is the only adopter in evidence, and this decision says so rather than presenting the hub's adopters as if they also validated the key.

**Fitness gates, applied before popularity.** No member is a crate, so the crate figures the prompt tabulates (90-day downloads, all-time downloads, last release, reverse dependencies, RustSec advisories) have no subject and are recorded `inapplicable` with that reason rather than filled with unrelated numbers. crates.io and RustSec were therefore not queried, deliberately.

| Gate | Verdict for all three members |
|---|---|
| 1. License compatible with `MIT OR Apache-2.0` | **Pass.** Every member is original repository content under the template's own license. Using a documented configuration key or file path creates no license obligation |
| 2. Crate and dependency-tree MSRV within the msrv-policy | **Inapplicable** — no crate, no dependency tree; nothing enters `Cargo.toml`, so `rust-version` is unaffected |
| 3. No open RustSec advisory; `unsafe` posture | **Inapplicable** — RustSec indexes crates.io packages and no member is one. No Rust code is added, so there is no `unsafe` posture to state |
| 4. Builds and is tested on `ubuntu-latest, macos-latest` | **Pass.** All three members are static text or JSON with no build step; the proposed acceptance checks use `git`, `jq` and `just`, available on both runners. Windows is noted, not required: `git ls-files` and `jq` behave identically and the announcement string is plain UTF-8 |
| 5. Default features and async-runtime coupling | **Inapplicable** — no Cargo features, no runtime |
| 6. Binary-size and compile-time cost | **Inapplicable** — nothing is compiled or linked. Repository cost, qualitatively: relative to a straight ts port this removes 3 files (roughly 60 lines) and adds 1 JSON key |

**Maintenance state of the reference artifacts** (rubric applied, not a release-age verdict). `agentsmd/agents.md`: `stargazers_count` 24268, `archived` false, `pushed_at` 2026-08-25T16:41:55Z, open issues 90 by the `search/issues` `total_count` rule, and 0 of the 10 most recently opened issues answered by an OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR (Opus, 2026-09-10). Verdict **stable-quiet**, not `at-risk`: the quiet tracker is a trigger to investigate, not a verdict, and the concrete `at-risk` signals are absent — the format is stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation, its normative content is a one-page convention with no code to rot, and its liveness is carried by vendor implementations rather than by repository activity. `anthropics/claude-code`: `stargazers_count` 144641, `archived` false, `pushed_at` 2026-09-10T06:06:11Z, open issues 11811 (Opus, 2026-09-10). Verdict **active**. Both figure sets are Opus's and are attributed rather than re-derived; the three individual issues both raws cite were re-read by this decision's check (Tier V, `## Engines`, disagreement 2).

**Migration implications — file-level effect on the template**, relative to a straight port of the ts precedent:

| Path | Action | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `.cursor/rules/projectenv.mdc` | **not created** | Cursor's current documentation presents root `AGENTS.md` as a rule type (Tier D for the loading behaviour); a pointer adds no instruction |
| `.cursor/rules/doc-template.mdc` | **not created**; its real documentation policy moves into `AGENTS.md` or `docs/` under F197 / R81 | It is a second policy source (B2), and its frontmatter no longer matches the documented `globs` form |
| `.windsurf/rules/justfile-rules.md` | **not created**; its `Justfile` conventions move into `AGENTS.md` | Vendor demotes the path to a fallback behind `.devin/rules/`, under a retired product name; content duplicates F177 / F178 |
| `.devin/rules/` | **not created** | The hub covers it, and nested `AGENTS.md` covers directory scoping |
| `.claude/settings.json` | **created, or extended** if another item creates it first for plugin enables, with `companyAnnouncements` as an array of exactly one string | F199; owner requirement recorded in D-024(6) |
| repository guard (name and location owned by P03) | **one new check block** asserting A2, A3, A4a and A4b | Without it the omission reverts silently the first time a vendor `init` wizard runs |
| `AGENTS.md` | **gains** the `Justfile` conventions inherited from ts's Windsurf rule, and a short note naming the tools known to read the file | Keeps the single policy source complete after the spokes are dropped. The file is F197's, not this item's |

Nothing enters `Cargo.toml`; no CI job is added beyond the repository-guard lane R11 owns; no crate is introduced.
